chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahbub, from 'Ali ibn Ri'ab, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said:
I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about the forearm, when it is struck and the wrist-bone is broken from it. He said, and then said:

"If the palm withers from it, and all the fingers of the palm become paralyzed, then in it there is two-thirds of the diyah, the diyah of the hand." He said: "And if some of the fingers become paralyzed while some remain, then for each finger that becomes paralyzed there is two-thirds of its diyah." He said: "And likewise is the ruling regarding the shin and the foot when the toes of the foot become paralyzed."

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This report does not conflict with the report narrated by al-Halabi that one-tenth of the diyah is due for the finger when it becomes paralyzed or is cut off, because we interpret the narration of al-Halabi as referring to one who does to it that by which it becomes paralyzed, so he becomes liable for two-thirds of the diyah, the diyah of the finger; then he cuts it off, so he becomes liable for one-third of its diyah by cutting off the paralyzed finger, and thus he completes its full diyah. According to this manner, there is no contradiction between the two reports.

key_terms.أَصَابِعُ: the fingers or toes whose paralysis has specified diyah
key_terms.الدِّيَةِ: the prescribed financial compensation for bodily injury
key_terms.الذِّرَاعِ: the forearm being discussed in the injury ruling
key_terms.الزَّنْدُ: the wrist-bone mentioned as broken by the strike
key_terms.السَّاقِ: the shin or lower leg to which the same rule is applied
key_terms.الْقَدَمِ: the foot whose toes are included under the same legal ruling
key_terms.الْكَفُّ: the palm or hand whose paralysis affects the ruling
key_terms.شَلَّتْ: became paralyzed or disabled in function

ai.seo_question: What is the diyah for a hand or fingers that become paralyzed due to injury in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out legal rulings for diyah in cases where injury to the forearm leads to paralysis of the hand or fingers, and it extends the same ruling to the leg and foot. It also includes Shaykh al-Tusi's reconciliation between two reports, explaining how compensation for paralysis and subsequent severing together amount to the full diyah of a finger.
